To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human liver slices are useful for studying the metabolism of xenobiotics in humans but should be used fresh, because the levels of cytochromes P450 decrease in culture.
human liver slices can be maintained in vitro for 3 days, and during that time, the major cytochrome P-450 enzymes decline at rates that vary widely, depending on which enzyme is being studied.
the major human cytochrome P-450 (CYPs) enzymes are maintained in precision-cut liver slices for different periods of time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a human liver slice model for the study of xenobiotic metabolism and toxicity in man.
the maintenance of the major cytochrome P-450 (CYP450) enzymes in cultured precision cut human liver slices (PHLSs) for 72h in supplemented RPMI-1640.
the maintenance of cytochromes P450 (Cyps) in precision-cut human slices cultured for up 72 h.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CYP1A, CYP2, and CYP2E enzymes are unstable in human liver slice culture, whereas CYP3A enzymes are stable.
the maintenance of CYP enzymes in precision-cut human slices is variable and unpredictable.
human liver slices are not suitable for long-term culture for the purpose of studying xenobiotic metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CYP2C, CYP3, and CYP2D enzymes are well maintained, whereas CYP1, CYP2, and CYP5 enzymes are not.
CYP enzymes can be divided into three groups: rapidly declining (CYP1A2 and CYP2A), intermediate (CYP2B6 and CYP2E), and relatively stable (CYP2C, CYP2 D, CYP3 A, and CYP 4A) in human liver slices.
human liver slice cultures are not a suitable model system for the study of drug metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are large differences in the stability of different CYP enzymes and that these differences are dependent on both the CYP enzyme and the liver donor.
there is no one medium that will maintain the levels of all CYP enzymes.
human precision-cut liver slices can be used to study drug metabolism in vitro but that the stability of the different CYP enzymes is very different.
